Στίχ. ʹ. Ἐὰν ἀναβῇ εἰς οὐρανὸν αὐτοῦ τὰ δῶρα· ἡ δὲ θυσία αὐτοῦ νεφῶν ἅψηται. Τοῦ
ἀσεβοῦς ἐὰν ἀναβῇ τὰ δῶρα εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, ἐὰν πάνυ ὑψωθῇ, ἐὰν ἡ θυσία αὐτοῦ
νεφῶν ἅψηται. Ὅτ' ἂν εὔξηται ὁ αἱρετικὸς, ὅτ' ἂν ἡ θυσία αὐτοῦ ἀναβῇ τῇ
ὑψηγορίᾳ, ὅτ' ἂν δοκῇ κατεστηρίχθαι· τότε εἰς τέλος ἀπολεῖται. Ἡ γὰρ εὐχὴ αὐτοῦ
λο γίζεται αὐτῷ εἰς ἁμαρτίαν, καὶ ἔστιν αὐτὴ ἡ εὐχὴ αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτία. Στίχ. ζʹ. Ὅταν
γὰρ δοκῇ ἤδη ἐστηρίχθαι, τότε εἰς τέλος ἀπολεῖται. Ὅμοιον, Οἱ δὲ ἐχθροὶ τοῦ Κυρίου
ἅμα τῷ δοξα σθῆναι καὶ ὑψωθῆναι, ἐκλείποντες ὡσεὶ καπνὸς ἐξέλιπον. Στίχ. ζʹ. Οἱ δὲ
ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐροῦσι· Ποῦ ἔστιν; Τίνες οἱ ἰδόντες αὐτόν; Οἱ ἐκκλησιαστικοὶ, οἱ
ἰδόντες ἐκείνων τὰ σφάλματα, ἐροῦμεν· Ποῦ ἔστιν; Στίχ. ηʹ. Ὥσπερ ἐνύπνιον
ἐκπετασθὲν οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ. Οἱ τοιοῦτοι ἐνυπνιαζόμενοι, καὶ ἀναπλάσσοντες
φαντάσματα, οὐ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ τὴν διάνοιαν ἐπερείδου σιν σφαλλόμενοι, καὶ γίνονται
ὥσπερ ἐνύπνιον ἐκπετασθὲν, ὃ οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ. Στίχ. ιʹ. Τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ ὀλέσαισαν
ἥττονες. Τοὺς υἱοὺς καὶ μαθητὰς τοῦ ταῦτα διδάξαντος. Στίχ. ιʹ. Αἱ δὲ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ
πυρσεύσαισαν ὀδύνας. Αἱ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ, φησὶν, τουτέστιν αἱ πράξεις, ἐξά ψουσιν
αὐτῷ κόλασιν. Αἱ δὲ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ. Τοῦ ἀσεβοῦς τούτου καὶ ἐσφαλμένου, οὗ ἡ
προσευχὴ λογίζεται εἰς ἁμαρ τίαν, οὗ ἡ θυσία ἐὰν ἀναβῇ εἰς οὐρανὸν, καὶ νε 17.73
φῶν ἅψηται, τότε εἰς τέλος ἀπόλλυται· τούτου αἱ χεῖρες ὀδύνας πυρσεύσουσι·
τουτέστι, καὶ ἐν ὀδύναις ἐσχάταις διάξουσι. Λέγει δὲ περὶ τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ πα ρανόμου.
Στίχ. ιγʹ. Χολὴ ἀσπίδος ἐν γαστρὶ αὐτοῦ. Ἔχει γὰρ μαθήματα, ἃ οὐκ ἔστι γλυκέα,
ἀλλὰ χολὴ ἀσπίδος, οἱονεὶ πονηρὰ, ἡ περὶ τοῦ οἴνου τῆς διδασκαλίας αὐτῶν. Ἐκ γὰρ
ἀμπέλου Σοδόμων ἡ ἄμπελος αὐτῶν, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα· Χολὴ δὲ ἀσπίδος ἐν
γαστρὶ τοῦ ἑτεροδόξου, καὶ ἀσεβοῦντος ἐν τοῖς δόγμασι, τοῖς ἐναντίοις τῇ ἀληθείᾳ.
Στίχ. ιεʹ. Πλοῦτος ἀδίκως συναγόμενος ἐξε μεθήσεται. Τίς γὰρ ἄλλος ἀδίκως πλοῦτος
συνάγεται ἢ ἐκεῖ νος ὁ ἐν τοῖς λόγοις αὐτῶν; Ἀδίκως γὰρ συνάγεται. Ἀλλ' ὁ ἀγαθὸς
οὐκ ἐάσει αὐτοὺς πεπτωκότας, πλοῦ τον ἀδίκως συναγόμενον ἔχειν ἀεὶ αὐτὸν ἐν
ἑαυτοῖς· ποιήσει γὰρ ἐξεμέσαι. Στίχ. ιεʹ. Ἐξ οἰκίας αὐτοῦ ἐξελκύσει αὐτὸν ἄγγελος.
Ἄγγελος γὰρ κατ' ἐνέργειαν καὶ εὐεργεσίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐξελκύσει αὐτὸν ἀπ' αὐτῆς τῆς
κακῶς οἰκοδο μηθείσης, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐκκλησία πονηρευομένων. Αὕτη γὰρ ἡ οἰκία
αὐτοῦ. Ἀλλ' ἄγγελος ἐξελκύσει αὐτὸν ἐξ οἰκίας αὐτοῦ. Στίχ. ιζʹ. Μὴ ἴδοι ἄμελξιν
νομάδων. Ἑτερόδοξος οὐ βλέπει ἄμελξιν νομάδων. Νο μάδες δὲ εἰσί τινες ψυχαὶ
νεμόμεναι ὑπὸ τῷ καλῷ Ποιμένι, τῷ εἰπόντι· Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα. ∆ι' ἐμοῦ ἐάν τις
εἰσέλθῃ, σωθήσεται. Καὶ εἰσελεύσεται, καὶ ἐξελεύσεται, καὶ νομὴν εὑρήσει. Στίχ. ιηʹ.
Ὥσπερ στρίφνος ἀμάσητος, ἀκατά ποτος. Οἱ λόγοι καὶ τὰ δόγματα στριφνὰ καὶ
πυκνὰ, οὐ δὲν ἔχει γλυκὺ ἐκεῖνα, τὰ κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ γινόμενα. Στρίφνος βοτάνη, τίς
ἐστιν ἐκτραχυνομένη τῇ γλώσσῃ τοῦ μασσωμένου. Ὥσπερ οὖν, φησὶ, τὴν βοτάνην
ἐκείνην, κἂν ἄγαν τις φιλονεικήσειε διαλεά νας τοῖς ὀδοῦσι, καταπιεῖν οὐ δύναται·
οὕτω καὶ ὁ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων ἀπολαύειν ἐθέλων οὐδὲν τῶν πόνων ἀποίσεται τὸ
κέρδος. Στίχ. κʹ. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἀνθήσει αὐτοῦ τὰ ἀγαθά. Ἂ δοκεῖ ἀγαθὰ ποιεῖν, οὐκ
ἀνθήσει· ὅτ' ἂν δοκῇ ἤδη πεπληρῶσθαι, θλιβήσεται. Στίχ. κʹ. Οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ
σωτηρία τοῖς ὑπάρχουσι. Τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ σωτηρίαν αὐτῷ περιποιῆσαι οὐ
δύναται. Ἄλλως. Στίχ. κβʹ. Πᾶσα δὲ ἀνάγκη αὐτὸν ἐπελεύσεται, καὶ ἐπαποστελεῖ ἐπ'
αὐτὸν θυμὸν ὀργῆς. Στίχ. κβʹ. Πᾶσα δὲ ἀνάγκη ἐπ' αὐτὸν ἐπελεύ σεται. Ταῦτα
προτρεπτικὰ ἡμῖν, ἵνα ἀφιστώμεθα τῶν ἀλλοτρίων. 17.76 Στίχ. κβʹ. Νίψαι ἐπ' αὐτὸν
ὀδύνας. Ἀντὶ νιφετοῦ ὀδύναι ἔρχονται ἐπὶ τὸν τοιοῦτον. Στίχ. κδʹ. Καὶ οὐ μὴ σωθῇ ἐκ
χειρὸς σιδήρου. Σίδηρον οὐ λέγει τοῦτον τὸν αἰσθητὸν, ἀλλὰ τμη τικώτατον λόγον.
pass_a_gloss: Verse (number lost). If his gifts go up into heaven, and his sacrifice touches clouds. Of the impious: if the gifts go up into heaven, if he is very much exalted, if his sacrifice touches clouds. Whenever the heretic prays, whenever his sacrifice goes up by lofty-speaking, whenever he seems to have been firmly fixed, then he will perish to the end. For his prayer is reckoned to him into sin, and his prayer itself is sin. Verse 7. For whenever he seems already to have been fixed, then he will perish to the end. Similar: but the enemies of the Lord, at the same time as being glorified and exalted, failing like smoke they failed. Verse 7. But those having seen him will say: where is he? Who are those having seen him? The churchmen, the ones having seen the errors of those men, we will say: where is he? Verse 8. Like a dream having flown out he will not be found. Such people, dreaming and moulding phantasms, do not prop the mind on the truth, being tripped up, and they become like a dream having flown out, which will not be found. Verse 10. His sons may lesser ones destroy. The sons and disciples of the one who taught these things. Verse 10. And his hands may they kindle pains. His hands, he says, that is the deeds, will kindle punishment for him. And his hands: of this impious and erring one, whose prayer is reckoned into sin, whose sacrifice if it goes up into heaven and touches clouds, then he perishes to the end; of this one the hands will kindle pains; that is, also in the last pains they will pass the time. He speaks about the sons of the lawless one. Verse 13. Gall of an asp in his belly. For he has teachings which are not sweet, but gall of an asp, as it were wicked, the one about the wine of their teaching. For from the vine of Sodom is their vine, and the following. And after a little: and gall of an asp in the belly of the other-opinioned one, and of the one being impious in the doctrines, the ones contrary to the truth. Verse 15. Wealth unjustly gathered will be vomited out. For what other wealth is unjustly gathered than that one in their words? For it is unjustly gathered. But the good one will not let them, having fallen, have always within themselves the wealth unjustly gathered; for he will make them vomit it out. Verse 15. Out of his house an angel will drag him. For an angel, according to the working and kindness of God, will drag him out from the very house badly built, which is an assembly of those doing evil. For this is his house. But an angel will drag him out of his house. Verse 17. May he not see a milking of grazing flocks. The other-opinioned one does not see a milking of grazing flocks. Grazing flocks are certain souls being pastured under the good Shepherd, the one who said: I am the door. Through me if anyone enters, he will be saved, and he will go in and will go out and will find pasture. Verse 18. Like a strifnos unchewed, unswallowable. The words and the doctrines tough and dense; those have nothing sweet, the things happening against God. Strifnos is a certain herb becoming rough on the tongue of the one chewing. So, as, he says, that herb, even if someone very much strives, grinding it with the teeth, cannot swallow; so also the one wanting to enjoy the things of others will carry off nothing of the gain of the labours. Verse 20. Because of this his good things will not bloom. The things he seems to do good will not bloom; whenever he seems already to have been filled, he will be afflicted. Verse 20. There is no salvation of his for his possessions. His possessions cannot procure salvation for him. Otherwise. Verse 22. And every constraint will come upon him, and he will send upon him fury of wrath. Verse 22. And every constraint will come upon him. These are exhortatory for us, so that we stand away from the things of others. Verse 22. May he snow pains upon him. Instead of snowfall, pains come upon such a one. Verse 24. And he will surely not be saved from a hand of iron. He does not say this perceptible iron, but a most cutting word.
pass_b_english: “If his gifts go up to heaven, and his sacrifice touches the clouds” (Job 20:6). This is the ungodly man: even if his gifts go up to heaven, even if he is lifted up very high, even if his sacrifice touches the clouds. Whenever the heretic prays, whenever his sacrifice goes up on the strength of his lofty talk, whenever he seems to have been set firm, then he will perish utterly. For his prayer is reckoned to him as sin, and his prayer itself is sin.

“For when he seems already to have been made firm, then he will perish utterly” (Job 20:7). It is like this saying: “But the enemies of the Lord, as soon as they are glorified and exalted, vanish away like smoke” (Psalm 37:20).
“And those who have seen him will say: Where is he?” (Job 20:7). Who are the ones who have seen him? We of the Church, who have seen the errors of those men, will say: Where is he?

“Like a dream that has flown away, he will not be found” (Job 20:8). People of this kind dream and fashion phantoms for themselves. Because they have gone astray, they do not rest their mind on the truth, and they become like a dream that has flown away and will not be found.

“May the lesser ones destroy his sons” (Job 20:10). His sons: that is, the sons and disciples of the man who taught these things. “And may his hands kindle pains” (Job 20:10). His hands, he says, that is, his deeds, will kindle punishment for him.

“And his hands”: the hands of this ungodly and erring man, whose prayer is reckoned as sin, whose sacrifice may go up to heaven and touch the clouds, and then he perishes utterly. This man's hands will kindle pains; that is, they too will pass their days in the utmost pains. He is speaking about the sons of the lawless man.

“The gall of an asp is in his belly” (Job 20:14). For he holds teachings that are not sweet but are the gall of an asp: something wicked, as it were, the gall that belongs to the wine of their teaching. “For their vine is of the vine of Sodom” (Deuteronomy 32:32), and so on.
And a little later: The gall of an asp is in the belly of the man who holds other doctrines and is ungodly in his teachings, those that are opposed to the truth.

“Wealth gathered unjustly will be vomited up” (Job 20:15). For what other wealth is gathered unjustly than the wealth that lies in their words? It is gathered unjustly. But the Good One will not allow them, fallen as they are, to keep the wealth gathered unjustly within themselves for ever; he will make them vomit it up.

“An angel will drag him out of his house” (Job 20:15). For an angel, by the working and the kindness of God, will drag him out of that very house which was badly built, which is a congregation of evildoers. That is his house. But an angel will drag him out of his house.

“May he not see the milking of the grazing flocks” (Job 20:17). The man who holds other doctrines does not see the milking of the grazing flocks. The grazing flocks are certain souls that feed under the good Shepherd, who said: “I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved, and he will go in and go out and find pasture” (John 10:9).

“Like a tough herb that cannot be chewed or swallowed” (Job 20:18). The words and doctrines that are set against God are tough and dense; there is nothing sweet in them. The strifnos is a plant that turns rough on the tongue of the one who chews it. So, he says, just as no one can swallow that plant, however hard he strives to grind it down with his teeth, so too the man who wants to enjoy what belongs to others will carry off no profit from all his labors.

“Therefore his good things will not blossom” (Job 20:21). The things he seems to do as good will not blossom; “when he seems already to have been filled, he will be afflicted” (Job 20:22). “There is no salvation for him in his possessions” (Job 20:20). His possessions cannot win salvation for him.

Otherwise: “And every distress will come upon him, and he will send upon him the fury of wrath” (Job 20:22-23). “And every distress will come upon him” (Job 20:22). These words urge us to keep away from what belongs to others.
“May he snow pains upon him” (Job 20:23). Instead of snow, pains come upon a man of this kind.
“And he will not be saved from the hand of iron” (Job 20:24). By iron he does not mean the iron our senses perceive, but a word that cuts most keenly.
